stories.title: Fund Administrator Hanover Park Inks 19K-SF Deal at 387 Park Avenue South
stories.excerpt: An artificial intelligence-driven fund administrator is moving its headquarters to TF Cornerstone’s 387 Park Avenue South, Commercial Observer has learned. Hanover Park signed a 19,269-square-foot lease on the entire 10th floor of the NoMad property, marking its fifth office move in two years, according to CEO Chris Hladczuk. The firm’s most recent office address is listed on its website as 115 East 23rd Street. TF Cornerstone did not immediately provide the asking rent or the length of the lease, but the average asking rent for office space in Midtown South was $85.73 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to a report from CBRE. “Existing tenants are choosing to expand here and new companies are choosing to locate here,” Joe Lanzilotta, director of commercial asset management at TF Cornerstone, said in a statement. “The property continues to outperform the market as a destination for growing businesses.” It is unclear who represented the tenant in the transaction, but Cushman & Wakefield’s Ethan Silverstein handled negotiations on behalf of the landlord in the deal signed in July. It’s unclear who represented the tenant. “The combination of TF Cornerstone’s long-term investment, highly efficient 20,000-square-foot floor plates and premier NoMad location continues to resonate with tenants,” Silverstein said in a statement. “The recent leasing activity demonstrates that companies are prioritizing best-in-class buildings, and with one full floor becoming available this fall, the property remains well positioned to meet continued demand.” Other recent deals in the 230,000-square-foot building at the corner of Park Avenue South and East 27th Street include a lease for marketing firm PMG Worldwide, which expanded from the second to third floor in May and brought its total footprint there to 38,744 square feet, according to TF Cornerstone. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Hanover Park (AI fund admin) leases 19.3K SF at 387 Park Avenue South, NoMad Manhattan
Midtown South office asking rent $85.73/SF Q2 2026; property outperforming market
Fifth office move in two years signals tenant churn and relocation activity
stories.summary: An artificial intelligence-driven fund administrator, Hanover Park, signed a 19,269-square-foot lease for the entire 10th floor at TF Cornerstone's 387 Park Avenue South in NoMad. The deal marks Hanover Park's fifth office move in two years. Midtown South office space was averaging $85.73 per square foot in Q2 2026, with the property described as outperforming the market as a destination for growing companies.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance. However, the rapid tenant churn (5 moves in 2 years) and continued office leasing in Midtown South despite broader NYC office headwinds suggests pockets of corporate demand and growth in specific Manhattan submarkets, which could signal underlying employment strength that supports rental demand in nearby residential buildings serving the same workforce.

stories.title: Ken Griffin, Vornado, Rudin to Form JV for $6B 350 Park Ave. Development
stories.excerpt: Vornado Realty Trust and Rudin Management have formally agreed to enter into a joint venture with an affiliate of Kenneth C. Griffin, Citadel’s founder and CEO (KG), to develop a 1.9-million-square-foot trophy office building at 350 Park Ave. In connection with the development, Citadel will lease 1.05 million square feet for 15 years as its primary New York office. The JV will be owned 60% by KG, 36% by Vornado and 4% by Rudin. The project is budgeted at approximately $6.2 billion, of which $3.3 billion will be financed through a construction loan. Vornado will serve as the developer, operating member, property manager and leasing agent. Vornado and KG will be the co-managing members and have joint control over decisions. On Vornado’s recent second-quarter earnings call, chairman and CEO Steven Roth dismissed claims from analysts that the REIT would be better off walking away from the deal, originally forged in 2024. “In our business, there is no better place to invest than prime Park Avenue with a million-square-foot tenant and a 60% partner already committed,” he said. The post Ken Griffin, Vornado, Rudin to Form JV for $6B 350 Park Ave. Development appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Citadel/Ken Griffin, Vornado, Rudin form JV for $6.2B 350 Park Ave office tower
Citadel leases 1.05M SF for 15 years; Griffin funds 60%, $3.3B construction financing
Major HQ expansion anchors trophy office development with institutional capital commitment
stories.summary: Kenneth C. Griffin's Citadel, Vornado Realty Trust, and Rudin Management formed a joint venture to develop a 1.9-million-square-foot office building at 350 Park Avenue in Manhattan. Citadel will lease 1.05 million square feet as its primary New York office for 15 years. The project is budgeted at $6.2 billion with $3.3 billion in construction financing; Griffin owns 60% of the JV, Vornado 36%, and Rudin 4%.
stories.impact: Signals sustained financial-services sector confidence in NYC real estate and employment base. Citadel's 15-year, 1M+ SF commitment anchors major capital deployment in Manhattan and reinforces the metro's draw for high-margin corporate tenants, underpinning resident demographic strength and rental demand in luxury and upper-midmarket residential buildings in Midtown and surrounding submarkets over the next decade.

stories.title: Vacant Arizona Center Office Tower Converting to JW Marriott Hotel
stories.excerpt: LaPour Partners plans to transform a once-thriving 19-story Phoenix office tower into a 340-room hotel. The Phoenix Business Journal reports the repurposed property at 400 E. Van Buren St. will be across the street from another signature hotel, the 1,000-room Sheraton Phoenix Downtown. Arizona Center was built in the early 1990s but has fallen into decline over the past 10 to 15 years. The $200 million JW Marriott will include new restaurants, a resort-style pool, fitness center, ballroom, meeting spaces and a club lounge on the upper levels of the property. It will also have approximately 15,000 square feet of meeting and ballroom space on the upper floors of the tower. Currently the Arizona Center office building is vacant, and the hotel project is in the design and pre-development phase. Interior demolition is expected to start in early 2027, with construction commencing later that year. The JW Marriott is expected to open in 2029. The post Vacant Arizona Center Office Tower Converting to JW Marriott Hotel appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: LaPour Partners converting vacant 19-story Phoenix office tower to 340-room JW Marriott
$200M hotel project at 400 E. Van Buren St.; interior demolition early 2027, opening 2029
Office-to-hotel conversion reflects Phoenix office vacancy; hospitality redevelopment trend
stories.summary: LaPour Partners is converting a vacant 19-story office tower at 400 E. Van Buren Street in Phoenix into a 340-room JW Marriott hotel with $200 million in investment. The property, built in the early 1990s, has declined over the past 10–15 years. Interior demolition is slated for early 2027, with construction to follow and opening expected in 2029. The hotel will include restaurants, a resort-style pool, fitness center, ballroom, and 15,000 square feet of meeting space.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact, but signals persistent Phoenix office market weakness and capital reallocation into hospitality. The office-to-hotel conversion removes distressed supply from the market and may improve near-term sentiment on downtown Phoenix real estate, supporting broader mixed-use development and potential residential recovery on the adjacent block near the 1,000-room Sheraton, though the 2029 opening is distant.

stories.title: Cawley CRE Completes 287K-SF Industrial Lease in West Chicago
stories.excerpt: Cawley Commercial Real Estate completed a 286,622-square-foot industrial lease at 1717 Harvester Road in West Chicago, Illinois. The long-term lease brings the 465,950-square-foot manufacturing facility to full occupancy. The Cawley CRE team, consisting of David Conroy, Mark Wilson, Jordan Kwiecinski, and Daniel Cawley, SIOR, represented the landlord, Plymouth REIT, in the transaction. The tenant, CoreCentric Solutions, was represented by Mike Senner of Colliers. The leased property offers 4,000 amps of heavy power, 15,579 square feet of office space, 14 interior docks, and one drive-in door, making it well-suited for advanced manufacturing and operational needs. The lease is scheduled to commence in October 2026. “This transaction reflects the continued demand for well-located, functional manufacturing facilities in the Chicago market,” said Conroy. “We are honored to continue our relationship with Plymouth REIT and appreciate the opportunity to help execute their leasing strategy at this property.” Join Brookfield Properties, Prologis, and Cushman & Wakefield | August 20The companies at the cutting edge of industrial real estate will gather for Connect Industrial West on August 20th in Irvine, CA. stories.impact: Not directly relevant to multifamily development. stories.title: Peachtree Recaps Ritz-Carlton Portland With $141M C-PACE Loan
stories.excerpt: A New York lender is more than ready for a Portland hospitality resurgence. Ready Capital, which assumed full ownership of the The Ritz-Carlton Portland mixed-use project following a foreclosure in July 2025, just secured $141 million of commercial property accessed clean energy (C-PACE) debt for the recapitalization of the 35-story tower, Commercial Observer has learned. Peachtree Group originated the C-PACE loan for the 2023-completed Block 216 Tower development that features a 251-key hotel, 131 condominium units and 159,000 square feet of office space. Construction of the Ritz-Carlton-Portland, the Marriott’s brand’s first hotel in the Pacific Northwest, commenced in 2019 before encountering delays due to the COVID-19 pandemic and ensuing struggles to the city’s economy. Jared Schlosser, head of credit originations at Peachtree Group, said condo units at the property have sold at a healthy pace and the hotel is well positioned for success as one of the newest lodging offerings in the Portland region. “It’s the nicest hotel up there and that pocket of Portland is revitalizing,” Schlosser told CO. “I think there’s probably more tailwinds ahead versus headwinds for Portland.” Schlosser added that C-PACE debt was conducive for the recap since as a newer building it was developed under “stringent” building codes with much of the project eligible for retroactive financing. He noted that the deal marks Peachtree’s second largest loan. Ready Capital set the stage for owning The Ritz-Carlton Portland when it acquired a prior construction loan on the development valued at more than $500 million through a 2022 merger with Mosaic Real Estate Investors. The lender manages the property in partnership with Lincoln Property Company. Ready Capital did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Ready Capital (foreclosure 7/2025) secures $141M C-PACE debt for Ritz-Carlton Portland
Block 216 Tower mixed-use: 251-key hotel, 131 condos, 159K SF office; 2023 completion
Hotel, condos, office experiencing recovery; condo sales pace healthy, hotel well-positioned
stories.summary: Ready Capital, which assumed full ownership of the Ritz-Carlton Portland following a foreclosure in July 2025, secured $141 million in commercial property assessed clean energy (C-PACE) debt for the recapitalization of the 35-story Block 216 Tower. The 2023-completed mixed-use property includes a 251-key hotel, 131 condominium units, and 159,000 square feet of office space. Jared Schlosler of Peachtree Group noted condo units are selling at a healthy pace and the hotel is well positioned as the Marriott brand's first in the Pacific Northwest.
stories.impact: Portland mixed-use recovery signal. The condo absorption strength within the Ritz-Carlton Portland asset and the resort's success as a new lodging anchor suggest improving downtown Portland demand and potential for nearby multifamily development to benefit from renewed visitor/business travel and residential in-migration, though the 2025 foreclosure underscores earlier pandemic distress in the market.

stories.title: Office Furniture Manufacturer Haworth Renews 30K SF at SL Green’s 125 Park Avenue
stories.excerpt: Office furniture manufacturer Haworth is staying seated at 125 Park Avenue. Haworth has signed a 10-year lease renewal for its 30,365-square-foot office and showroom space at the 25-story Midtown office building, landlord SL Green Realty announced Wednesday. The company, which manufactures and sells high-end, ergonomic office seating and workspaces, has been a tenant in the property, also known as the Pershing Square Building, for more than a decade. The firm, which did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s request for comment, previously renewed its lease for the same space back in 2015, CO reported at the time. The asking rent was $100 per square foot. SL Green was represented in-house in this deal, while Haworth was represented by Ethan Silverstein and Amy Zhen from Cushman & Wakefield. C&W did not immediately respond to a request for comment. “We are proud to extend our valued relationship with Haworth at 125 Park Avenue,” Steven Durels, executive vice president and director of leasing and real property at SL Green, said in a statement. “The building’s proximity to Grand Central Terminal and our new lobby and elevator cab renovation have helped maintain 99 percent occupancy.” SL Green acquired 125 Park Avenue in 2010 for $330 million, according to property records. The building sits across the street from Grand Central Terminal on Park Avenue and East 42nd Street. Other tenants in the building include banking and investment firm TD Securities and real estate brokerage Newmark. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Haworth renews 30.4K SF office/showroom at SL Green's 125 Park Avenue for 10 years
Haworth a tenant 10+ years; prior renewal in 2015; Midtown Manhattan retention
Furniture manufacturer commitment reflects stable NYC office demand, prime location
stories.summary: Office furniture manufacturer Haworth renewed its 30,365-square-foot lease for 10 years at SL Green Realty's 125 Park Avenue (Pershing Square Building), a 25-story Midtown office building. Haworth has been a tenant for more than a decade and previously renewed for the same space in 2015. The property is positioned near Grand Central Terminal with recent lobby and elevator upgrades.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. Renewal of a long-term design/manufacturing tenant signals stable Midtown Manhattan office fundamentals and employer retention, supporting residential demand from office workers in adjacent and nearby multifamily buildings in Midtown and Flatiron submarkets.

stories.title: CBRE Promotes Anna Wolke (Faktorow) and Stuart Dyer in the Firm’s Data Center Solutions Group
stories.excerpt: CBRE announced that Anna Wolke (Faktorow) and Stuart Dyer have been promoted to executive vice president within the firm’s Data Center Solutions Group. Based in Northern Virginia, Wolke and Dyer advise developers, investors, institutional owners and occupiers across the U.S. data center sector. Alongside their team, they have played a role in some of the industry’s most significant transactions. Collectively, Wolke, Dyer and team have completed more than $28 billion in capital markets transactions and 45 powered land transactions valued at more than $2.1 billion. “The explosive growth of cloud computing and digital infrastructure is reshaping the data center sector, creating both new opportunities and new complexity for our clients,” said Kyle Schoppmann, President, CBRE Mid-Atlantic. “Anna and Stu have been instrumental in helping clients navigate that growth while contributing to the continued expansion of our Data Center Solutions business.” Wolke specializes in advising data center developers, investors and institutional owners on capital markets and strategic real estate transactions. Dyer advises clients across the artificial intelligence, cloud and federal sectors on data center occupancy and development strategies. The post CBRE Promotes Anna Wolke (Faktorow) and Stuart Dyer in the Firm’s Data Center Solutions Group appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: CBRE promotes Wolke and Dyer to EVP in Data Center Solutions Group, Northern Virginia base

stories.summary: CBRE announced promotions of Anna Wolke (Faktorow) and Stuart Dyer to executive vice president within its Data Center Solutions Group, based in Northern Virginia. The two and their team have completed more than $28 billion in capital markets transactions and 45 powered land transactions valued at over $2.1 billion. The promotion reflects explosive growth in cloud computing and digital infrastructure reshaping the data center sector.
stories.impact: Data center and AI infrastructure boom is a major multifamily demand driver in Northern Virginia and adjacent markets (Northern CA, Texas, etc.). Rapid capital deployment in powered land acquisition and data center development signals large-scale employer expansion in these regions, increasing both employment density and in-migration of technical talent, which directly supports multifamily rental growth and development feasibility in data center–adjacent submarkets.

stories.title: CMBS Loan Backed by Vornado, Related’s 85 10th Avenue Sent to Special Servicing
stories.excerpt: A $396 million commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) loan secured by 85 10th Avenue, a 633,000-square-foot office property in Manhattan’s Chelsea neighborhood, has been sent to special servicing due to imminent maturity default, according to an alert from Morningstar Credit. 85 10th Avenue is owned jointly by Vornado Realty Trust and the Related Companies. Related purchased the property in 2007 from Somerset Partners for $430 million and brought Vornado in as a 50/50 partner. The $396 million loan makes up DBWF 2016-85T and is part of larger conduits CD 2017-CD3 and BACM 2017-BNK3. It is expected to default ahead of its December 2026 maturity date, according to Morningstar. The building’s largest tenant, Google, currently takes up 47 percent of its space, as the firm has gradually expanded since signing a 180,000-square-foot lease in 2014. But cash flow from rents has declined lately, particularly since the COVID-19 pandemic. Morningstar Credit reports that 85 10th Avenue’s cash flow fell 28 percent below underwriting in 2025, and that biometric screening company CLEAR, which signed a 120,000-square-foot lease for a new headquarters in 2021, is currently in a rent abatement period. Vornado reported that the building’s occupancy stood at 89 percent in its most recent second-quarter earnings supplemental. The 11-story 85 10th Avenue first opened in 1913 as a Nabisco factory and was redeveloped for commercial office use in the late 1990s. Vornado and Related invested into renovating the lobby in 2023. Vornado and Related did not respond to requests for comment. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: $396M CMBS loan on 85 10th Avenue (Vornado/Related) sent to special servicing
633K SF Chelsea office; Google is 47% tenant; maturity default imminent (December 2026)
Cash flow declined since COVID; iconic Manhattan office facing refinance stress
stories.summary: A $396 million CMBS loan backed by 85 10th Avenue, a 633,000-square-foot office property in Manhattan's Chelsea neighborhood owned by Vornado Realty Trust and Related Companies, has been sent to special servicing due to imminent maturity default. Google occupies 47% of the space after gradually expanding since a 2014 lease. Cash flow has declined significantly since the COVID-19 pandemic, and the loan is expected to default ahead of its December 2026 maturity.
stories.impact: Major trophy office asset distress in Chelsea underscores ongoing Manhattan office market weakness and refinance headwinds for even prime assets with large-cap tenants. Potential asset-level distress and restructuring could signal broader capital constraints and cap-rate pressure on office-heavy portfolios, tightening debt availability for mixed-use and multifamily development in NYC and reinforcing a structural shift in office space utilization that benefits adjacent multifamily properties serving smaller, distributed tenant bases rather than single large employers.

stories.title: Newgard Group Buys West Palm Dev Site to Build Car-Centric Private Club
stories.excerpt: Harvey Hernandez’s Newgard Group bought a development site in West Palm Beach, Fla., to build an upscale parking garage with a private members club component. The Miami-based developer paid $10.5 million for a 2.6-acre parcel at 2500 North Florida Mango Road, just north of Palm Beach International Airport, property records show. Called Palm Beach Auto Haus, the upcoming two-story development will be a private members club with space to park 20 cars and amenities that include padel courts, coworking lounges, a cafe and a gym. The project marks somewhat of a departure for a new-to-market developer in West Palm Beach, most of whom have launched luxury condo developments near the city’s waterfront. “For years I searched for a place that reflected the way passionate automobile enthusiasts truly enjoy their collections,” Hernandez, founder and CEO of Newgard Group, said in a statement. “We envisioned something far beyond traditional car storage — a destination centered around ownership, design, community and unforgettable experiences.” Newgard Group nabbed a $6.3 million acquisition loan from Belmont Bank & Trust. The seller, a Thousand Oaks, Calif.-based entity tied to Jonathan and Justin Bergman, had purchased the asset, which holds a 29,790-square-foot commercial building, for $3.5 million in 2021. The Bergmans could not be reached for comment. In Miami’s Brickell district, Newgard Group is building a waterfront, luxury condo complex alongside Two Roads Development, after securing a $513 million debt package last year. Earlier this month, it sold off a piece of land for $50 million to another development team. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Newgard Group acquires 2.6-acre West Palm Beach site for $10.5M (2500 N Florida Mango Rd)
Palm Beach Auto Haus: private members club, 20-car parking, padel, coworking, cafe, gym
Niche luxury development north of Palm Beach International Airport; departure from waterfront trend
stories.summary: Newgard Group purchased a 2.6-acre development site in West Palm Beach at 2500 North Florida Mango Road for $10.5 million to build Palm Beach Auto Haus, a two-story private members club with 20-car parking, padel courts, coworking lounges, a cafe, and a gym. The development is located just north of Palm Beach International Airport and marks a departure from typical West Palm Beach waterfront luxury condo developments.
stories.impact: Limited multifamily relevance. Niche automotive-lifestyle development signals affluent demographic interest in experiential, non-residential amenities in West Palm Beach's airport-adjacent submarket, but does not directly compete with or support multifamily development. May indirectly attract high-income residents to the northern West Palm Beach area, creating secondary demand for adjacent luxury rental housing.

stories.title: After 30-Year Hold, Monarch Offloads Golden Apartment Community
stories.excerpt: Monarch Investment & Management Group sold Fox Hill Apartments, a 153-unit garden-style community in Golden, Colorado for $32 million. Monarch Investment & Management Group owned Fox Hill for nearly 30 years. Sierra Parkway Communities was the buyer. JLL represented Monarch in the sale of the property. JLL Capital Market’s Sales and Advisory team was led by Jordan Robbins, Wick Kirby, Alex Possick and Seth Gallman. JLL asserts that the 1972-built property at 17611 W. 16th Ave. presents a value-add opportunity, with the ability to renovate 100% of its unit interiors to a standardized scope while enhancing outdoor amenity spaces. The average in-place rent of $1,645 sits significantly below the area’s $908,000 median home price, creating a 3.30-times premium to own versus rent within a one-mile radius. Current rent levels represent just 15% of average household incomes exceeding $128,000 in the immediate area. The property maintains 95% occupancy and has averaged 96% occupancy since 2021. The post After 30-Year Hold, Monarch Offloads Golden Apartment Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Monarch Investment offloads Fox Hill Apartments (153 units, Golden CO) after 30-year hold for $32M

stories.summary: Monarch Investment & Management Group sold Fox Hill Apartments, a 153-unit garden-style community in Golden, Colorado, to Sierra Parkway Communities for $32 million after owning the property for nearly 30 years. The 1972-built property at 17611 W. 16th Avenue maintains 95% current occupancy (average 96% since 2021) and has in-place rents of $1,645, significantly below the area's median home price of $908,000. The property presents a value-add opportunity with potential to renovate 100% of unit interiors and enhance amenities.
stories.impact: Colorado Front Range multifamily asset transition signals value-add opportunity in 50-year-old garden-style stock. Below-market rent positioning ($1,645 in an area with $128K+ household incomes and strong owner-occupancy premium) suggests significant upside for new operator via unit renovation, property-level capex, and rent growth—typical acquisition profile for growth-oriented multifamily operators. Robust occupancy despite age indicates resilient demand in Golden, supporting broader development feasibility in metro Denver markets with demographic and employment tailwinds.
